newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end mixed, outperform U.S. issues.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end mixed, outperform U.S. issues.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed mixed on Monday, but performed better than their U.S. counterparts, as modest strength in the Canadian dollar helped encourage investors, analysts said.

"There was a tendency to outperform through the day and I think that's just based on the currency doing a bit better and people just feeling a bit less nervous about where the currency might be going," said Jim Webber, director of fixed-income research with TD Securities Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.23 to C$108.40 to yield 7.276 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 14/32 to yield 7.09 percent. The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 19 basis points from 20 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.

The Canadian dollar ended stronger at C$1.3985 (US$0.7150) on Monday from Friday's close at C$1.3995 (US$0.7145). Dealers said initial gains were prompted by European buying overnight. The currency's strength in turn helped strengthen the prices of T-bills and short-term bonds.
The long end of the yield curve was hurt by weaker U.S. Treasuries, which ended lower in light trade as traders set up shorts ahead of U.S. bond auctions.
